response.justification: The candidate is an experienced full-stack/web software engineer (15+ years) with strong craftsmanship, testing, and distributed-systems skills, but the resume shows essentially no overlap with the core requirements of a Principal Performance Architect for AI accelerators. There is no SoC or IP modeling, no RTL/architectural simulation, no GPU/SIMD/MIMD architecture work, and no deep-learning training or inference optimization experience. The closest adjacencies — C/C++ at National Instruments, low-latency D services at Sociomantic, and some robotics/embedded exposure — are software-level performance work, not hardware-software co-design. Educationally, a BS with 8+ years meets the minimum bar, but the domain gap is too large for a principal-level hardware architecture role.
strengths: 15+ years of broad engineering experience across embedded, backend, and systems work
Demonstrated low-latency, high-throughput performance work (millions of req/s at Sociomantic)
C/C++ background at National Instruments plus strong testing and tooling discipline
concerns: No SoC/IP modeling, RTL, or hardware architecture simulation experience
No deep-learning training/inference optimization or GPU/SIMD/MIMD workload analysis
Career trajectory is web/full-stack, not principal-level silicon performance architecture

key_factors.factor: Missing SoC/IP modeling and hardware co-design
No AI accelerator or DNN workload optimization background
Extensive senior software engineering and low-latency performance experience
